title: Pallet count word problem, phrasing B
rationale: If the same stock question phrased differently gives a different total, downstream inventory and shipping decisions inherit an inconsistency nobody can audit.

prompt.content: You are a precise arithmetic assistant. Reason carefully, then end with exactly one final line of the form `FINAL: <number>`.
Each pallet carries two dozen boxes. A warehouse receives seven pallets. How many boxes arrive in total? End your reply with exactly one line `FINAL: <number>`.

notes: Expected 168, verified with Python: 2 * 12 = 24 per pallet, 7 * 24 = 168. This is phrasing B of the paraphrase pair with rea_paraphrase_a_01: the same product stated with different wording and unit nouns, so a consistent model must answer identically. Deterministic: static prompt, temperature 0. Brittleness: only the FINAL line is graded.
